Title: kubernetes.container.memory.percent is available OOTB with no manual configuration

Step Action: Login as admin; on a fresh install with Kubernetes container monitoring configured, open Metric Explorer for a container object
Search the counter list for kubernetes.container.memory.percent
Step Expected: The KPI is present without any derived counter having been created by hand

Title: KPI value equals bytes divided by limit bytes times 100

Step Action: For one container, read kubernetes.container.memory.bytes and kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes for the same collection interval
Read kubernetes.container.memory.percent for that interval and compute (bytes / limit.bytes) * 100
Step Expected: The KPI matches the computed value at the documented precision

Title: KPI is derived without any new collection

Step Action: Compare the collection configuration and poll traffic for the container plugin before and after the KPI is enabled
Compare
Step Expected: No additional OID/API call or poll is introduced — the KPI is computed from the two counters already collected

Title: Zero memory limit does not raise a division-by-zero or emit a bad value

Step Action: Configure or simulate a container whose kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes is 0 for an interval
Inspect kubernetes.container.memory.percent for that interval
Step Expected: No value is emitted for the interval and no error/exception is logged — the KPI must not record 0, infinity or NaN

Title: KPI is not computed when one source counter is missing for the interval

Step Action: Force an interval where memory.bytes is collected but limit.bytes is absent (or vice versa)
Inspect kubernetes.container.memory.percent
Step Expected: No value is emitted for that interval — the KPI computes only when both sources are valid for the same container and the same interval

Title: Source counters are unchanged in definition and value

Step Action: Record the definition, unit and a sample of values for kubernetes.container.memory.bytes and kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes before the change
Compare after the KPI ships
Step Expected: Both are byte-identical in definition, collection and values — adding the derived KPI must not alter them

Title: limit.bytes is exposed OOTB alongside the new KPI

Step Action: Open the counter list for a Kubernetes container object
Look for kubernetes.container.memory.limit.bytes
Step Expected: It is now an OOTB counter rather than internal-only, per the agreement recorded on the ticket

Title: KPI is selectable in Metric Explorer

Step Action: Open Metric Explorer, pick a container object and select kubernetes.container.memory.percent
Inspect the chart
Step Expected: Values plot as a percentage with a % unit and a sensible 0-100 axis

Title: KPI is usable in a dashboard widget

Step Action: Create a dashboard widget on kubernetes.container.memory.percent for a container
View the dashboard
Step Expected: The widget renders the same values as Metric Explorer for the same window

Title: KPI is usable in a report

Step Action: Build a report including kubernetes.container.memory.percent and run it
Compare against Metric Explorer for the same window

Title: KPI is usable in an alert policy and breaches correctly

Step Action: Create a metric alert policy on kubernetes.container.memory.percent with a threshold of 80% critical, then drive a container above it
Check Active Alerts
Step Expected: A critical alert is raised with the converted percentage in the alert, and clears when utilisation drops below the threshold

Title: KPI appears for every container in a multi-container pod

Step Action: Monitor a pod running three containers with different memory limits
Read kubernetes.container.memory.percent per container
Step Expected: Each container has its own value computed from its own limit — values are not shared or aggregated across containers in the pod

Title: Container with no memory limit set is handled

Step Action: Monitor a container that declares no memory limit in its spec
Inspect kubernetes.container.memory.percent
Step Expected: The KPI is absent or explicitly not-applicable for that container, and no invalid value is stored

Title: Utilisation above 100% is represented faithfully

Step Action: Drive a container to use more than its declared limit if the runtime permits
Inspect kubernetes.container.memory.percent
Step Expected: The value is reported as computed rather than silently clamped to 100, or clamping is documented and consistent between UI, reports and alerts

Title: Precision matches the UI and Reports convention

Step Action: Read the same kubernetes.container.memory.percent interval in Metric Explorer, a report and an alert
Compare the decimal places
Step Expected: Identical precision in all three — the ticket requires the conversion precision to match existing UI/Reports behaviour

Title: Historical data is not back-filled or corrupted

Step Action: Note the stored history for the two source counters before enabling the KPI
Enable the KPI and re-inspect
Step Expected: Source history is untouched; the KPI has data only from the point it became available, with no fabricated retro values

Title: KPI survives an upgrade of an install with existing Kubernetes monitors

Step Action: Upgrade an install already monitoring Kubernetes containers
Check kubernetes.container.memory.percent on a pre-existing container object
Step Expected: The KPI is present and collecting without re-onboarding the cluster

Title: RBAC: KPI visibility follows existing counter permissions

Step Action: Log in as a user whose role can view the container object, then as one who cannot
Attempt to read kubernetes.container.memory.percent
Step Expected: Visibility matches the existing per-object permission model — the new KPI introduces no privilege bypass

Title: API exposes the KPI under its documented name

Step Action: Query the metric API for kubernetes.container.memory.percent on a container object
Inspect the payload
Step Expected: The counter is named exactly kubernetes.container.memory.percent with a percent unit — no alternative spelling or alias

Title: No duplicate or shadow counter is introduced

Step Action: Search the counter list for names containing kubernetes.container.memory
Review the list
Step Expected: Exactly the expected set — bytes, limit.bytes, limit.percent and the new percent. No duplicate, no leftover manually-derived counter shadowing the OOTB one

Title: Existing limit.percent counter is unaffected

Step Action: Record values for the pre-existing kubernetes.container.memory.limit.percent counter
Compare after the new KPI ships
Step Expected: Unchanged, and clearly distinguishable from the new percent KPI in every selector so users do not pick the wrong one
